content.text:
**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

The IP/data direction in this agreement runs our way and satisfies the **preferred** checklist in full:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Customer owns Deliverables/work product | § 14.2 (with § 1.4 defining Deliverable as work product created specifically for Customer) |
| Vendor assigns Deliverables | § 14.2 — "Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest," plus personnel assignments |
| Vendor retains pre-existing IP | § 14.3 + § 1.8 (Vendor Technology = pre-existing, excludes Customer Data and Customer's pre-Effective-Date IP) |
| Licence to embedded Vendor IP perpetual / irrevocable / royalty-free | § 14.3 routes to § 13.2: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" |
| Customer retains all rights in Customer Data | § 14.1 |
| Vendor licence in Customer Data limited to processing to provide the Services | § 14.1 ("solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer") reinforced by § 15.1 |
| No joint ownership | § 14.4 (none created absent a separate instrument both Parties sign) |

Key judgment calls: (i) the § 14.1 "provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer" formulation is service delivery, not independent exploitation, so no narrowing edit is warranted; (ii) § 15.1's "without Customer's express written consent" is a consent gate, not a standing Vendor licence, so it is not flagged; (iii) the § 14.3 cross-reference to § 13.2 resolves to real operative text, so there is no dangling reference to cure.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not redlined under IP: § 13.1's revocable, Affiliate/contractor-excluding **Services** licence (a LICENSE issue) and § 11.1's immediate-deletion language (a TRANSITION issue). Neither is an ownership or Customer Data assignment defect, and flagging them here would double-count terms owned by other rules.
